card.name: Partway through words, before predictable continuation
card.fires_on: Fires on the word 'be' after 'should', and on word pieces inside long names or terms (Hypercort-icism, Yasuk-uni, ep-igen-etic) where the rest of the word or phrase is highly predictable.

modes.label: 'be' after should
modes.description: The word 'be' following 'should' in instructions, where a past participle comes next.
modes.example: Precautions to reduce the risk of falls should<< be>> taken, particularly for patients with motor impairment

modes.label: Inside long names and terms
modes.description: A middle piece of a rare name or medical term, with the ending nearly certain to follow.

modes.label: Second word of a known phrase
modes.description: A noun completing a familiar phrase such as 'political economy' or 'adrenal suppression'.
modes.example: considerably less adrenal<< suppression>> following a single morning dose of prednis
